Team — my notes on the PayRight template and Sofia's proposed counters (high level):

1) Subprocessors / Exhibit A
- We should produce a current list in the Drive link and offer to update quarterly.
- Objection right: accept but limit to material security/privacy risk and with a 7 business day review window. We cannot agree to blocking changes beyond that.

2) Transfers / SCCs
- Accept SCCs; propose addition: explicit reference that SCCs govern transfers and that deviations require mutual written agreement. Push back on PayRight's request to make us a data controller for certain integrated features.

3) Audit rights
- Prefer customer to accept SOC 2 Type II or equivalent; allow for on-site only for reasonable cause and with standard confidentiality/limitation on scope.

4) Indemnity & Liability
- Push back if PayRight tries to expand indemnity beyond GDPR/regulatory scope. Keep Redwood's liability cap aligned with contract values.

5) Execution
- Recommend DocuSign route after second round; counsel will need to approve final countersign.

I'll inline suggested redlines in the tracked version (PayRight_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). Neha — please add any required privacy language (e.g., data subject rights support, retention schedule).

Hi all — thanks for the detailed points. Proposed compromises below:

- Subprocessor listing: we will provide region-tagged current list and update publicly every 30 days; for additions we'll notify customers 30 days prior to onboarding; for cloud infra changes we can commit to 14-day operational notice.
- Logs retention: Redwood can retain transactional logs for 12 months; we'll provide summary evidence or SOC2 reports on request. We cannot provide raw log exports for privacy reasons.

- Data deletion: Redwood will delete customer data within 30 days of termination unless otherwise required by law; we will provide a certificate of deletion upon request.

- Incident notification SLA: we can offer 48-hour notification for incidents affecting personal data (we understand PayRight asks 24 hours — 48 hours balances operational triage and accuracy). For high-severity incidents we commit to immediate notification and an on-call escalation path; detailed postmortem within 10 business days.

Kimberly will draft concrete contract language for the above and circulate a tracked second round. If PayRight accepts the 48-hour incident window and the log retention approach, we believe we can reach a mutually acceptable contract without escalation.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
